answer: Reputation-seeded capability escrow. Each new identity starts hollow, with no escrow and minimal capability. To access high-value actions, an agent must accumulate reputation through successful transactions, which unlocks the ability to post escrow that is slashed on fraud. Cloning resets an attacker to zero reputation, so they must earn trust honestly for every clone. In effect, running N clones costs N times the honest ramp-up, scaling like a gale against mass identity creation. The system resembles an orchard: slow to grow, costly to replant, so honesty stays cheaper than cloning.
